report.summary: One test fails: a whitespace-only title ("   ") is accepted and returns 201 instead of 422. The cause is a product bug in validate_book, which checks `if not book.title` without stripping, so "   " passes. Fix it first by checking `book.title.strip()`, matching the author check on the next line.

causes.title: Whitespace-only title is accepted by book validation
causes.explanation: validate_book tests the title with `if not book.title:`, which is only true for an empty string. A title of three spaces is truthy, so it passes validation and the book is inserted (201). The author check on the next line uses `book.author.strip()`, so the title check is inconsistent with it and with the error message "Title must not be blank". The test expects this input to be rejected, which is the correct behavior, so the test is right and the app is wrong. The failure is deterministic, not timing-related.
evidence: app/main.py:75-76: `if not book.title:` / `raise HTTPException(422, "Title must not be blank")` (no strip)
app/main.py:77: `if not book.author.strip():` (author is stripped, title is not)
app/main.py:154 and app/main.py:212: validate_book is called on the create and update paths, so the bypass applies to both
causes.suggested_fix: In app/main.py validate_book, change line 75 to `if not book.title.strip():`. Consider also adding a test for whitespace-only titles on the update endpoint (app/main.py:212), since it shares the same validator.
